Workplace
(1) Prepare a clean, well-lit workspace without static electricity, prepare screwdrivers and pliers.
(2) When performing the subsequent component assembly steps, remove the relevant components from the packaging and remove the protective films, if any.
1. Installing the CPU into the motherboard
(1) Place the motherboard on a flat surface (such as the motherboard packaging box).
(2) Locate the CPU socket and lift the side lever all the way up. On Intel motherboards, the metal protective cover will also lift up with the lever.
(3) Hold the CPU by the edges (without touching the contacts on the bottom) and align the marked raised corner of the CPU with the corner of the socket.
(4) Carefully insert the CPU into the socket without any pressure or effort.
(5) Lower the lever back down. The Intel CPU may pop off the protective plastic cover of the CPU socket.
(6) Make sure the CPU is inserted straight.
2. Installing the M.2 SSD
(1) Locate the M.2 slot (usually between the CPU and PCIe slots).
(2) If a radiator is installed on top, unscrew it and remove the protective film from it.
(3) Insert the M.2 SSD into the slot at an angle of about 30 degrees and gently press the other end of the SSD down.
(4) Replace the radiator if present and secure it with a screw. If there is no radiator, simply secure the M.2 SSD with a screw.
3. Installing the CPU cooler
(1) Install the cooler mount (according to the cooler instructions and available parts)
(2) If there is no thermal paste applied to the CPU cooler, apply a small amount to the CPU and spread evenly.
(3) Remove the protective film from the base of the CPU cooler, place the cooler on the CPU, and screw it in diagonally (crosswise).
(4) Connect the cooler cable to the CPU_FAN connector on the motherboard.
4. Installing the RAM

(1) Check the number of RAM slots on the motherboard. If there are 2 slots, RAM can be installed in one or both. If there are 4 slots, modules are usually installed in pairs (for example, in slots 1 and 3 or 2 and 4).
(2) Open the latches on both ends of the RAM socket or on one side until they are fully open.
(3) Hold the RAM module by the edges and align its contacts with the protrusion in the socket.
(4) Carefully insert the module into the slot and press it down until it clicks into place.
5. Installing the motherboard into the case
(1) Open the case and check the mounting bars (expansion screws). If they are not installed, screw them in according to the motherboard type (ATX, Micro-ATX, Mini-ATX) and the case manual.
(2) Locate and install the rectangular plug (metal plate) on the back of the case, making sure it clicks into place and the smooth surface of the plug faces outward from the case.
(3) Insert the motherboard into the case, aligning the ports with the plug sockets and retaining bars.
!!! Make sure that the protrusions of the plug do not enter into the ports on the motherboard.
(4) Secure the motherboard with screws (screw them diagonally) without overtightening.
(5) Locate the front panel cables and connect them to the F_PANEL connectors on the motherboard (usually on the lower right side), following the motherboard diagram.
(6) Pay attention to:
- The polarity of PWR_SW and RESET_SW is not important;
- Be sure to observe the correct polarity (+/-) of the LED;
- Connect audio and USB cables according to the keys and shape of the jacks.
6. Installing the SSD/HDD
(1) Insert the HDD or SSD into the appropriate slot in the case (3.5″ HDD - in the slot at the bottom of the case, 2.5″ SSD - in the special bracket behind the motherboard).
(2) Align the drive with the mounting holes and secure it with screws or other fasteners.
(3) Connect the SATA data cable to the drive and the other end to the SATA data connector on the motherboard.
7. Installing case cooler
(1) If your computer case supports the installation of additional coolers, install the coolers in the designated locations (front, rear, or top).
(2) Screw them in place with screws, taking into account the airflow direction. Connect the cooler cable to the motherboard connector SYS_FAN
8. Installing PSU
(1) Insert the PSU into the designated location in the case (usually at the back, bottom or top), place the cooler down.
(2) Align the screw holes and secure the PSU with the included screws.
9. Cables connection
(1) Connect the 24-pin ATX cable to the main power connector of the motherboard (usually located on the right side near the RAM). Make sure the latch is properly secured.
(2) Connect the 4-pin or 8-pin (4+4) CPU cable to the CPU power connector located next to the CPU socket.
(3) Connect the SATA power cables to the HDD and SSD drives.
(4) Make sure all cables are fully inserted and organize the cables using the plastic tie wraps.
10. Installing GPU
(1) Locate the GPU socket plugs on the back of the case, remove them and save the screws.
(2) Hold the GPU by the edges and align it with the PCIe x16 slot on the motherboard.
(3) Carefully insert the GPU into the socket until it clicks and screw it to the case using the plug and screws.
(4) Connect the appropriate PCIe 6-pin or 8-pin (6+2) power cable from the PSU.
